newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Rubin argues for balanced budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Rubin argues for balanced budget pact.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin dismissed talk that the strong U.S. economy erases the need for a balance budget agreement and stressed the importance of such a pact.

In an interview on Cable News Network, when asked if the robust economy replaces the need for a balanced budget accord, Rubin said: "I don't agree with that. I think the very good conditions we've had over the last five years have come from a strategy of deficit reduction and all the effects that has on economic growth."
"I think we need to stay with that strategy -- finish the job and put in place the balanced budget agreement."
Rubin also rejected recent politicians' assertions that the budget will move into surplus due to the strength of the economy and that further tax cuts could result.
"I don't think we should depend on what might or might not happen and I think that is relatively unlikely to happen -- a surplus -- without a deficit reduction program.
Rubin was not asked and made no statement regarding foreign exchange levels or the dollar.
